classification.difficultyReason: Link rounded handspan measurements to a self-organised frequency table and choose an axis covering the collected data. Then identify extremes and the most common length and construct the dot plot; the measurement procedure and sequence are supplied.

content.prompt: [Class activity] Record the length of the handspan of each member of your class, correct to the nearest centimetre. Spread the fingers and thumb fully and measure from the tip of the little finger to the tip of the thumb.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw up a frequency table of the results.

answer.short: Answers vary. A frequency table showing each recorded handspan in centimetres and its frequency.
answer.worked: Measure each class member’s handspan from the little-finger tip to the thumb tip, to the nearest centimetre. Tally the measurements, then record the frequency of each length. Check that the total frequency equals the number of class members measured.

answer.short: Answers vary: the smallest recorded handspan, in centimetres.
answer.worked: Read the smallest handspan with a non-zero frequency in the class table. State the length in centimetres.

answer.short: Answers vary: the largest recorded handspan, in centimetres.
answer.worked: Read the largest handspan with a non-zero frequency in the class table. State the length in centimetres.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the most commonly occurring length of handspan in your class?

answer.short: Answers vary: the handspan length or lengths with the greatest frequency, in centimetres.
answer.worked: Compare the frequencies in the class table. Report the length with the greatest frequency, or all tied lengths if more than one has that frequency.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Draw a dot plot for the data.

answer.short: Answers vary. A labelled dot plot of the class handspans.
answer.worked: Draw an equally spaced numerical axis labelled “Handspan (cm)” covering the recorded lengths. Place one dot for each class member above their recorded length, stacking repeated lengths vertically. Check that each stack matches the table and the total number of dots equals the number measured.
